description: The count channel's multiplicity is half the carrier's crossing count, so with the owner-ruled Hopf pair carrier (c2 = 2) the ratio b3/b2 = c3/2 - 3 lives on a lattice. The measured 0.6411239316 falls in a gap: the nearest integer carrier assignment misses by 16.98%. All four carrier rules the corpus derives give b3/b2 <= 0. Exact rational arithmetic, no free parameters.

unconstrained.note: BOTH nearest points are ODD and are EXCLUDED once the carrier is Brunnian -- see 'brunnian_parity'

brunnian_parity.constraint: n+ = n- => c = n+ + n- is EVEN

straddle_trap.c2_from: owner ruling A 2026-08-29, Hopf deuteron carrier
straddle_trap.verdict: NOT a result -- two different carrier assignments

assertions.name: measured b3/b2 is the exact rational 950815/1483044
assertions.detail: r = 950815/1483044; matches the Lean constant rMeasured

assertions.name: every consistently-read rule gives b3/b2 <= 0
assertions.detail: min-length -2, chain -1, canonical Brunnian 0, census -11/6; measured is +0.6411

assertions.name: the canonical Brunnian carriers sit EXACTLY on the degenerate locus
the straddle (Hopf c2=2 with census c3=7) manufactures the sign
assertions.detail: straddled = 1/2 (+ sign, -22.01% off) but census read CONSISTENTLY = -11/6; the two crossing numbers come from different carrier assignments

assertions.name: NO integer carrier assignment reproduces the measured b3
assertions.detail: scanned the half-integer grid n in [2,12] and the quarter-integer grid m in [8,20]; the Lean proves it for ALL integers (no_quarter_lattice_point_is_measured)

assertions.name: the finest lattice still misses by 161468/1483044 (16.98%)
assertions.detail: gap = 40367/370761 = 0.108876 in b3/b2 units, 16.98% of the measured value; matches the Lean bound in quarter_lattice_gap

assertions.name: the single-carrier grid misses by more (22.01%), as a sublattice must
escaping the gap needs c3 > 6, ABOVE the minimal Brunnian 3-braid
assertions.detail: QOU.Knots.KauffmanTL3 machine-checks that no braid word of length < 6 is both Brunnian and nontrivial, so 6 is minimal; with parity the next available value is c3 = 8, not 7

assertions.name: the Brunnian parity constraint EXCLUDES both previously-nearest points
assertions.detail: the unconstrained nearest were c(3H)+c(3He) = 15 and c3 = 7, BOTH ODD, hence unreachable by carriers with n+ = n-; parity is not a refinement of the bound, it deletes the two points the bound was attained at

assertions.name: under parity the gap WIDENS to 209293/1483044 (22.01%)
assertions.detail: gap = 209293/1483044 = 0.141124, 22.01% of measured -- up from the 16.98% that ignoring parity allows; matches the Lean bound in even_lattice_gap

assertions.name: a SINGLE Brunnian A=3 carrier makes b3/b2 an integer, nearest +55.98%
assertions.detail: c3 even => b3/b2 = c3/2 - 3 is an integer; nearest positive is 1 at c3 = 8, +55.98%, and 0 at the Borromean c3 = 6 is the degenerate locus

scope: (b) on the CONJUNCTION {count channel, mu = c/2, Hopf pair carrier c2 = 2, integer crossing counts}, with the invariant named: integrality of a crossing count. (a) on every ingredient separately -- it excludes neither the count channel, nor the Brunnian mechanism (brunnian_binding_survives untouched), nor mu = c/2. Releasing any one reopens it.
caveats: CONDITIONAL ON OWNER RULING A (2026-08-29). The obstruction exists only because c2 is pinned. CountChannelCarrierLocus correctly records that with mu_pair FREE the count channel has ample freedom and no quantisation argument applies; that retraction is not reversed, its hypothesis is now supplied.

The cheapest escape is dropping mu = c/2: a multiplicity that is not half a crossing count is not lattice-valued, and the obstruction evaporates. This probe does not argue for mu = c/2 -- it takes it from CountChannelCarrierLocus.countChannel.

The census row is AME-INVERTED by the atlas registry's own admission and is NOT a derivation. It appears here only to show that even it gives the wrong sign when read consistently, so the circularity is not what rescues the sign -- the straddle is.
b3 uses the isospin-averaged Bbar(3). If 3H and 3He carry different links the grid refines from half- to quarter-integer, which is the case computed; it does not become dense.
Three body orders is three data points, and b4 is not tested here at all. Nothing about A > 4 follows.

The Brunnian parity constraint applies to the A >= 3 carriers only. The A = 2 Hopf carrier is NOT Brunnian (lk = 1, n+ = 2, n- = 0) -- it is the boundary case where lk = z = 1 -- so c2 = 2 is even for a different reason and nothing here depends on that.

The range where the answer could differ (word length >= 8) has NEVER been searched: the enumeration ran at L_K_max = 3-4, and L <= 8 over 4 inter-nucleon generators is ~87,000 words against the ~84 that were tried. This probe does not run that search; it establishes that the search is the open question.
source: AME2020 total nuclear binding energies; integer crossing counts
